headline: Bonds and oil keep nerves raw even as stocks claw back losses
body: Equities closed last week on a firmer note -- the Dow added close to 1% and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each rose roughly 0.4% Friday -- but that bounce only partly offset a rough stretch in which chip names fell more than 4% and the Nasdaq shed close to 2% on the week. The bigger story sits in the bond market: 30-year Treasury yields pushed to their highest level since 2007, near 5.3%, as investors weigh heavy government borrowing, AI-capex-driven debt issuance, and inflation that keeps running above target. The Treasury's move to expand long-bond buyback operations reads as an acknowledgment that the 'bond vigilante' dynamic is real. Layer in Middle East-linked oil strength, which is adding to inflation risk through the Strait of Hormuz supply constraints, and the tape looks more like relief than conviction.

Risk appetite showed up loudest in crypto: bitcoin surged roughly 22% over the week to top $78,000, with ether and XRP participating too and a chunk of ETF inflows skewed toward institutional buyers rather than a single speculative squeeze. Retail chatter on Reddit and WallStreetBets stayed concentrated in mega-cap AI and momentum names -- Nvidia, Amazon and Meta drew heavy mention volume, while Tesla's jump in Reddit buzz tracked its best weekly stock performance since spring. That split -- bonds and rate-sensitive sectors staying tense while crypto and a handful of favorite stocks rally hard -- suggests sentiment is bifurcated rather than uniformly greedy or fearful. With the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium and new Chair Kevin Warsh's first keynote just days away, positioning looks tentative, leaning on hope for a dovish signal rather than settled conviction.
